author: nflaig
content:
<@554799849288105986> re https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/630#discussion_r3694113770, so we don't repeat that discussion in multiple places

Allowing users to configure per-builder `min_bid` and `builder_booost_factor` for p2p builders is one of the open questions we need to resolve. I am generally one of the people that wants to make p2p options as on par as over api but that seems also questionable to me considering how p2p bid filtering works.

what in particular bothers me about it is that we overload the `builder_pubkey` field on the keymanager config which adds complexity for something that might be mostly useless. we do have `min_bid` and `builder_booost_factor` global config, so those would apply to p2p as well but only to the highest bid, for example in lodestar we have an api on the pool which just returns the best bid for `(bid.slot, bid.parent_block_hash, bid.parent_block_root)`, we filter bids beforehand because we anyways only need the highest one for the tuple, but that no longer works if you can boost or filter bids there locally via `min_bid`, on top of that, we do not even know the pubkey of the builder right now, we would need to resolve it again, our pool just keep the raw bid, with the builder index only.

so I believe <@346498651553660928> already voiced his opinion on it and is in favor of not supporting it, right? also would keep the `url` required param which is kinda nice on the config side

<@755590043632140352> from your comments
> but I do appreciate that indeed the boost in particular is kinda a stupid thing to have for p2p bids in a per-builder level, perhaps all are, min-bid, etc.
> Yes the boost is kinda irrelevant for p2p bids since they are filtered by nodes that don't know the proposer's value.
it seems you also think it's somewhat pointless

no need to discuss this now, but I wanna conclude this on ACDT ideally

author: ethdreamer
content:
There's a similar problem with `min_bid` applied to gossip bids. The whole point is that the user can have different `min_bid` values for different builders. There is a scenario:

`bid_A.valur < bid_B.value`
`bid_A.value > Builder_A.min_bid`
`bid_B.value < Builder_B.min_bid`

In this scenario, the cache evicts `bid_A` and holds `bid_B` even though the `min_bid` settings received later at proposal time make `bid_A` acceptable and reject `bid_B`

author: ethdreamer
content:
So under the current design, all of the settings:
- `min_bid`
- `builder_boost_factor`
- `max_execurion_payment`
Either don't apply to gossip bids or can't be properly applied because they aren't known before the cache filters them out

author: ethdreamer
content:
I see only two options:
1. Builder settings only apply to bids directly requested at proposal time
2. We send the extra information ahead of time when we send `BuilderPreferences`

author: nflaig
content: yeah I left a similar comment (less detailed) somewhere about this, can't find it now, but the outcome would be random based on p2p bid propagation

author: nflaig
content: `min_bid` and `builder_boost_factor` should be kept as global values and you would apply them to the highest bid you have in the p2p bid pool

author: ethdreamer
content: Well they can be properly applied to direct bids.

author: nflaig
content: (2) I don't get, why you need to send `min_bid` and `builder_boost_factor` beforehand? it's also local only, never forwarded to the builder

author: nflaig
content: global and per-builder override, but only for `url` (direct via api) builders

author: ethdreamer
content: You could in theory have a separate cache that applies the `boost` and `min_bid` settings properly to every bid it sees on gossip if those settings are known ahead of time. You would still need to keep track of the unboosted highest bid for gossip filtering. And you may still never see bids you would accept on gossip, because they were never the unboosted frontrunner so they were filtered on gossip.

author: ethdreamer
content:
But if you know the `min_bid` and `builder_boost_factor` ahead of time, you can just cache:
1. highest `bid.value` I've seen
2. highest boosted bid I've seen that also survives my `min_bid` setting

author: nflaig
content: if we would wanna make these values public, then you could add them to `ProposerPreferences` and make it part of `execution_payload_bid` gossip validation rules, ie. every node in the network applies `min_bid` and `boost` per the proposer preferences, for the local only approach, I just don't like that the outcome is random and unpredictable

author: ethdreamer
content: I don't think that works at all. Gossip rules become incoherent. You can't forward a bid based on whether any node in the network would boost it to the winner. At that point we would just remove the highest value filtering entirely

author: nflaig
content: I am not suggesting this btw, just floating the idea, i think it opens up some dos risks too, haven't really thought about it too much
